evidence: The project has a clear directory-based modularity (tools/, visualization/, solution/) with self-contained submodules for object_detection, pose_estimation, and solution-specific use cases (e.g., body, hand, wholebody)
All components are in a single Python package (rtmlib) with shared dependencies, no external communication boundaries (e.g., no REST/gRPC), and no deployment separation
Core logic is organized into cohesive modules with well-defined responsibilities; classes like RTMPose, Wholebody, and Hand combine object detection and pose estimation components internally
High cohesion within modules (e.g., pose_estimation/ includes all inference-related components: pre/post_processings and model wrappers)

Low coupling: fan-out is modest (avg 2.78), and dependency graph is mostly internal; tools depend on base and utility modules but not across domains (e.g., solution/ uses only object_detection/ and pose_estimation/ via imports)
The solution modules (e.g., Body, Hand) serve as facade components combining underlying detector/estimator tools without enforcing external interfaces
risks: Potential for accidental tight coupling if solution modules directly import internal model implementations instead of base/abstraction interfaces
No runtime separation or fault isolation — failure in one module could affect all others
Scalability limitations: cannot scale individual components independently (e.g., pose estimation vs. visualization)
Testing complexity increases as modules are tightly integrated in imports (e.g., Hand imports RTMDet and RTMPose directly)
